raw: CHAPTER II. The Grindstone
en: [Chapter 2]

raw: Tellson’s Bank, established in the Saint Germain Quarter of Paris, was in a wing of a large house, approached by a courtyard and shut off from the street by a high wall and a strong gate.
en: The Grindstone Tellson’s Bank in Paris was located in a wing of a large house, accessible through a courtyard and shut off from the street by a high wall and a strong gate.

raw: The house belonged to a great nobleman who had lived in it until he made a flight from the troubles, in his own cook’s dress, and got across the borders.
en: The house belonged to a great nobleman who had lived there until he fled the revolution, disguised in his cook's clothes, and crossed the border.

raw: A mere beast of the chase flying from hunters, he was still in his metempsychosis no other than the same Monseigneur, the preparation of whose chocolate for whose lips had once occupied three strong men besides the cook in question.
en: Running away like a wild animal fleeing hunters, he was still the same proud lord who once required three strong men besides that cook just to prepare his morning chocolate.

raw: Monseigneur gone, and the three strong men absolving themselves from the sin of having drawn his high wages, by being more than ready and willing to cut his throat on the altar of the dawning Republic one and indivisible of Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, or Death, Monseigneur’s house had been first sequestrated, and then confiscated.
en: With the lord gone, and his three servants clearing their consciences of serving him by declaring themselves ready to cut his throat for the new Republic of Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, or Death, the nobleman's house was first seized and then taken by the government.

raw: For, all things moved so fast, and decree followed decree with that fierce precipitation, that now upon the third night of the autumn month of September, patriot emissaries of the law were in possession of Monseigneur’s house, and had marked it with the tri-colour, and were drinking brandy in its state apartments.
en: Everything moved so fast, and new laws were passed so quickly, that by the night of September third, revolutionary officials were occupying the house, marking it with the tri-color flag, and drinking brandy in its elegant rooms.

raw: A place of business in London like Tellson’s place of business in Paris, would soon have driven the House out of its mind and into the Gazette.
en: If the London office of Tellson's had looked like the Paris branch, it would have driven the British managers crazy and forced them into bankruptcy.

raw: For, what would staid British responsibility and respectability have said to orange-trees in boxes in a Bank courtyard, and even to a Cupid over the counter?
en: For what would serious, respectable British businessmen think of orange trees in boxes in the courtyard, or a statue of Cupid over the counter?

raw: Yet such things were.
en: Yet those things existed in Paris.

raw: Tellson’s had whitewashed the Cupid, but he was still to be seen on the ceiling, in the coolest linen, aiming (as he very often does) at money from morning to night.
en: Tellson's had painted over the Cupid, but it could still be seen on the ceiling, aiming its bow at money from morning to night.

raw: Bankruptcy must inevitably have come of this young Pagan, in Lombard-street, London, and also of a curtained alcove in the rear of the immortal boy, and also of a looking-glass let into the wall, and also of clerks not at all old, who danced in public on the slightest provocation.
en: In serious London, such a decoration, along with a curtained alcove in the back, a mirror on the wall, and young clerks who danced in public, would have spelled ruin.

raw: Yet, a French Tellson’s could get on with these things exceedingly well, and, as long as the times held together, no man had taken fright at them, and drawn out his money.
en: Yet the French branch of Tellson's got along with these features just fine, and as long as times were stable, no one had been scared into withdrawing their money.

raw: What money would be drawn out of Tellson’s henceforth, and what would lie there, lost and forgotten; what plate and jewels would tarnish in Tellson’s hiding-places, while the depositors rusted in prisons, and when they should have violently perished; how many accounts with Tellson’s never to be balanced in this world, must be carried over into the next; no man could have said, that night, any more than Mr.
en: No one that night could say how much money would be withdrawn from Tellson's from now on, or how much would lie there lost and forgotten; what gold and jewels would tarnish in the bank's vaults while their owners rotted in prisons or died violent deaths; or how many accounts would never be settled in this world. Mr.

raw: Jarvis Lorry could, though he thought heavily of these questions.
en: Jarvis Lorry couldn't answer these questions either, though he was thinking deeply about them.

raw: He sat by a newly-lighted wood fire (the blighted and unfruitful year was prematurely cold), and on his honest and courageous face there was a deeper shade than the pendent lamp could throw, or any object in the room distortedly reflect--a shade of horror.
en: He sat by a newly lit wood fire, for the poor harvest year had brought an early winter cold, and his honest face showed a deep shadow of horror that was not caused by the hanging lamp or any reflection in the room.

raw: He occupied rooms in the Bank, in his fidelity to the House of which he had grown to be a part, like strong root-ivy.
en: In his loyalty to the bank, Mr. Lorry lived in rooms inside the building, having become as much a part of the place as ivy on a wall.

raw: It chanced that they derived a kind of security from the patriotic occupation of the main building, but the true-hearted old gentleman never calculated about that.
en: It happened that his rooms were somewhat protected because the patriots had taken over the main building, but the honest old gentleman never thought about his own safety.

raw: All such circumstances were indifferent to him, so that he did his duty.
en: He only cared about doing his duty.

raw: On the opposite side of the courtyard, under a colonnade, was extensive standing--for carriages--where, indeed, some carriages of Monseigneur yet stood.
en: On the opposite side of the courtyard, under a roofed walkway, was a parking area for carriages, where some of the nobleman's carriages still sat.

raw: Against two of the pillars were fastened two great flaring flambeaux, and in the light of these, standing out in the open air, was a large grindstone: a roughly mounted thing which appeared to have hurriedly been brought there from some neighbouring smithy, or other workshop.
en: Two large, burning torches were tied to the pillars, and in their light, out in the open air, stood a large grindstone. It was a rough machine that looked like it had been hurriedly brought there from a nearby blacksmith's shop.

raw: Rising and looking out of window at these harmless objects, Mr.
en: Standing up and looking out the window at these objects, Mr.

raw: Lorry shivered, and retired to his seat by the fire.
en: Lorry shivered and went back to his seat by the fire.

raw: He had opened, not only the glass window, but the lattice blind outside it, and he had closed both again, and he shivered through his frame.
en: He had opened both the glass window and the wooden shutter outside, closed them both again, and shuddered from head to toe.

raw: From the streets beyond the high wall and the strong gate, there came the usual night hum of the city, with now and then an indescribable ring in it, weird and unearthly, as if some unwonted sounds of a terrible nature were going up to Heaven.
en: From the streets outside the high wall and the gate came the usual night sounds of the city, but with a strange, eerie tone now and then, as if terrible, unusual noises were rising up to the sky.

raw: “Thank God,” said Mr.
en: “Thank God,” said Mr.

raw: Lorry, clasping his hands, “that no one near and dear to me is in this dreadful town to-night.
en: Lorry, folding his hands, “that no one I love is in this dreadful town tonight.

raw: May He have mercy on all who are in danger!”
en: May God have mercy on everyone in danger!”

raw: Soon afterwards, the bell at the great gate sounded, and he thought, “They have come back!” and sat listening.
en: Soon after, the gate bell rang, and he thought, “They have come back!” and sat listening.

raw: But, there was no loud irruption into the courtyard, as he had expected, and he heard the gate clash again, and all was quiet.
en: But there was no loud crowd rushing into the courtyard as he had expected; he heard the gate shut again, and everything went quiet.

raw: The nervousness and dread that were upon him inspired that vague uneasiness respecting the Bank, which a great change would naturally awaken, with such feelings roused.
en: His nervousness and fear made him anxious about the bank's security, which was a natural worry in such times.

raw: It was well guarded, and he got up to go among the trusty people who were watching it, when his door suddenly opened, and two figures rushed in, at sight of which he fell back in amazement.
en: The bank was well guarded, and he stood up to check on the guards when his door suddenly opened and two people rushed in. At the sight of them, he stepped back in absolute shock.

raw: Lucie and her father!
en: It was Lucie and her father!

raw: Lucie with her arms stretched out to him, and with that old look of earnestness so concentrated and intensified, that it seemed as though it had been stamped upon her face expressly to give force and power to it in this one passage of her life.
en: Lucie held her arms out to him with a look of intense, desperate seriousness, looking as if her face had been molded just to show this strength at this single moment of her life.

raw: “What is this?” cried Mr.
en: “What is this?” cried Mr.

raw: Lorry, breathless and confused. “What is the matter?
en: Lorry, breathless and confused. “What is the matter?

raw: Lucie!
en: Lucie!

raw: Manette!
en: Manette!

raw: What has happened?
en: What happened?

raw: What has brought you here?
en: What brought you here?

raw: What is it?”
en: What is going on?”

raw: With the look fixed upon him, in her paleness and wildness, she panted out in his arms, imploringly, “O my dear friend!
en: Staring at him wildly, pale and terrified, she gasped in his arms, pleading, “Oh, my dear friend!

raw: My husband!”
en: My husband!”

raw: “Your husband, Lucie?”
en: “Your husband, Lucie?”

raw: “Charles.”
en: “Charles.”

raw: “What of Charles?”
en: “What about Charles?”

raw: “Here.
en: “Here.”

raw: “Here, in Paris?”
en: “Here, in Paris?”

raw: “Has been here some days--three or four--I don’t know how many--I can’t collect my thoughts.
en: “He has been here a few days, three or four, I don't know, I can't think straight.

raw: An errand of generosity brought him here unknown to us; he was stopped at the barrier, and sent to prison.”
en: A generous mission brought him here without our knowledge. He was stopped at the border and sent to prison.”

raw: The old man uttered an irrepressible cry.
en: The old man let out a cry he couldn't stop.

raw: Almost at the same moment, the bell of the great gate rang again, and a loud noise of feet and voices came pouring into the courtyard.
en: Almost at the same instant, the gate bell rang again, and the sound of many feet and voices poured into the courtyard.

raw: “What is that noise?” said the Doctor, turning towards the window.
en: “What is that noise?” the Doctor asked, turning toward the window.

raw: “Don’t look!” cried Mr.
en: “Don't look!” Mr.

raw: Lorry. “Don’t look out!
en: Lorry cried. “Don't look out!

raw: Manette, for your life, don’t touch the blind!”
en: Manette, for your life, don't touch the shutter!”

raw: The Doctor turned, with his hand upon the fastening of the window, and said, with a cool, bold smile:
en: The Doctor turned, with his hand on the window lock, and said with a calm, confident smile:

raw: “My dear friend, I have a charmed life in this city.
en: “My dear friend, I am safe in this city.

raw: I have been a Bastille prisoner.
en: I was a prisoner in the Bastille.

raw: There is no patriot in Paris--in Paris?
en: There is no patriot in Paris, or in all of France, who would hurt me if they knew that.

raw: In France--who, knowing me to have been a prisoner in the Bastille, would touch me, except to overwhelm me with embraces, or carry me in triumph.
en: In France, if someone knew I used to be a prisoner in the Bastille, who would ever dare hurt me? Instead, they'd overwhelm me with hugs or carry me in triumph.

raw: My old pain has given me a power that has brought us through the barrier, and gained us news of Charles there, and brought us here.
en: My past suffering has given me a status that brought us through the border, got us news of Charles, and brought us here.

raw: I knew it would be so; I knew I could help Charles out of all danger; I told Lucie so.--What is that noise?” His hand was again upon the window.
en: I knew it would be this way. I knew I could save Charles from danger, and I told Lucie so. What is that noise?” His hand went back to the window.

raw: “Don’t look!” cried Mr.
en: “Don't look!” Mr.

raw: Lorry, absolutely desperate. “No, Lucie, my dear, nor you!” He got his arm round her, and held her. “Don’t be so terrified, my love.
en: Lorry cried out in desperation. “No, Lucie, my dear, don't you look either!” He wrapped his arm around her and held her tight. “Don't be so scared, my love.

raw: I solemnly swear to you that I know of no harm having happened to Charles; that I had no suspicion even of his being in this fatal place.
en: I swear to you that I don't know of any harm coming to Charles, and I had no idea he was even in this dangerous city.

raw: What prison is he in?”
en: Which prison is he in?”

raw: “La Force!”
en: “La Force!”

raw: “La Force!
en: “La Force!

raw: Lucie, my child, if ever you were brave and serviceable in your life--and you were always both--you will compose yourself now, to do exactly as I bid you; for more depends upon it than you can think, or I can say.
en: Lucie, my child, if you have ever been brave and helpful, and you have always been both, you must calm down now and do exactly as I tell you. More depends on this than you can imagine.

raw: There is no help for you in any action on your part to-night; you cannot possibly stir out.
en: You cannot help him by doing anything tonight; you cannot go outside.

raw: I say this, because what I must bid you to do for Charles’s sake, is the hardest thing to do of all.
en: I say this because what I must ask you to do for Charles's sake is the hardest thing of all: you must be obedient, still, and quiet.

raw: You must instantly be obedient, still, and quiet.
en: Let me put you in a back room.

raw: You must let me put you in a room at the back here.
en: You must leave your father and me alone for two minutes.

raw: You must leave your father and me alone for two minutes, and as there are Life and Death in the world you must not delay.”
en: Since this is a matter of life and death, you must not delay.”

raw: “I will be submissive to you.
en: “I will do as you say.

raw: I see in your face that you know I can do nothing else than this.
en: I can see in your face that you know I have no other choice.

raw: I know you are true.”
en: I know you are a true friend.”

raw: The old man kissed her, and hurried her into his room, and turned the key; then, came hurrying back to the Doctor, and opened the window and partly opened the blind, and put his hand upon the Doctor’s arm, and looked out with him into the courtyard.
en: The old man kissed her, hurried her into his bedroom, and locked the door. Then he ran back to the Doctor, opened the window, pushed the shutter slightly open, put his hand on the Doctor's arm, and looked out with him into the courtyard.

raw: Looked out upon a throng of men and women: not enough in number, or near enough, to fill the courtyard: not more than forty or fifty in all.
en: He looked out at a crowd of men and women. There weren't enough of them to fill the courtyard—maybe no more than forty or fifty people in total.

raw: The people in possession of the house had let them in at the gate, and they had rushed in to work at the grindstone; it had evidently been set up there for their purpose, as in a convenient and retired spot.
en: The patriots occupying the building had let them through the gate, and they had rushed in to use the grindstone. It had been set up there for them, as it was a convenient and private spot.

raw: But, such awful workers, and such awful work!
en: But what terrifying workers they were, doing such a terrifying job!

raw: The grindstone had a double handle, and, turning at it madly were two men, whose faces, as their long hair flapped back when the whirlings of the grindstone brought their faces up, were more horrible and cruel than the visages of the wildest savages in their most barbarous disguise.
en: The grindstone had handles on both sides, spun madly by two men. Their long hair flew back as they turned, revealing faces more horrible and cruel than those of wild warriors in war paint.

raw: False eyebrows and false moustaches were stuck upon them, and their hideous countenances were all bloody and sweaty, and all awry with howling, and all staring and glaring with beastly excitement and want of sleep.
en: They had glued on fake eyebrows and mustaches, and their ugly faces were covered in sweat and blood, twisted as they howled, their eyes wide with animal excitement and lack of sleep.

raw: As these ruffians turned and turned, their matted locks now flung forward over their eyes, now flung backward over their necks, some women held wine to their mouths that they might drink; and what with dropping blood, and what with dropping wine, and what with the stream of sparks struck out of the stone, all their wicked atmosphere seemed gore and fire.
en: As these thugs turned the stone, their messy hair flying about, some women held wine to their lips to let them drink. Between the dripping blood, the spilling wine, and the sparks flying from the stone, the whole scene seemed made of fire and blood.

raw: The eye could not detect one creature in the group free from the smear of blood.
en: Not a single person in the crowd was free from bloodstains.

raw: Shouldering one another to get next at the sharpening-stone, were men stripped to the waist, with the stain all over their limbs and bodies; men in all sorts of rags, with the stain upon those rags; men devilishly set off with spoils of women’s lace and silk and ribbon, with the stain dyeing those trifles through and through.
en: Pushing each other to get to the stone next were men shirtless to the waist, with blood smeared all over their bodies; men in rags stained with blood; and men wearing stolen women's lace, silk, and ribbons, all dyed with blood.

raw: Hatchets, knives, bayonets, swords, all brought to be sharpened, were all red with it.
en: Hatchets, knives, bayonets, and swords brought to be sharpened were all covered in red.

raw: Some of the hacked swords were tied to the wrists of those who carried them, with strips of linen and fragments of dress: ligatures various in kind, but all deep of the one colour.
en: Some of the bent swords were tied to the owners' wrists with strips of cloth torn from clothing, all stained the same deep red color.

raw: And as the frantic wielders of these weapons snatched them from the stream of sparks and tore away into the streets, the same red hue was red in their frenzied eyes;--eyes which any unbrutalised beholder would have given twenty years of life, to petrify with a well-directed gun.
en: As the frantic people grabbed their weapons from the sparks and ran back into the streets, their eyes glowed with the same red madness. Any normal person watching would have given twenty years of life to stop them with a gun.

raw: All this was seen in a moment, as the vision of a drowning man, or of any human creature at any very great pass, could see a world if it were there.
en: All of this was seen in a single second, like the quick flash of images a drowning man sees.

raw: They drew back from the window, and the Doctor looked for explanation in his friend’s ashy face.
en: They stepped back from the window, and the Doctor looked at his friend's pale face for an explanation.

raw: “They are,” Mr.
en: “They are,” Mr.

raw: Lorry whispered the words, glancing fearfully round at the locked room, “murdering the prisoners.
en: Lorry whispered, looking fearfully toward the locked bedroom door, “murdering the prisoners.

raw: If you are sure of what you say; if you really have the power you think you have--as I believe you have--make yourself known to these devils, and get taken to La Force.
en: If you are sure of what you said, if you really have the influence you think you have, and I believe you do, go show yourself to these monsters and have them take you to La Force.

raw: It may be too late, I don’t know, but let it not be a minute later!”
en: It might be too late already, but don't waste another second!”

raw: Doctor Manette pressed his hand, hastened bareheaded out of the room, and was in the courtyard when Mr.
en: Doctor Manette squeezed his hand, ran out of the room without a hat, and was already in the courtyard by the time Mr.

raw: Lorry regained the blind.
en: Lorry reached the shutter again.

raw: His streaming white hair, his remarkable face, and the impetuous confidence of his manner, as he put the weapons aside like water, carried him in an instant to the heart of the concourse at the stone.
en: His flowing white hair, his striking face, and his confident manner as he pushed the weapons aside allowed him to reach the center of the crowd by the grindstone immediately.

raw: For a few moments there was a pause, and a hurry, and a murmur, and the unintelligible sound of his voice; and then Mr.
en: For a few moments, the crowd paused, murmured, and listened to his voice. Then Mr.

raw: Lorry saw him, surrounded by all, and in the midst of a line of twenty men long, all linked shoulder to shoulder, and hand to shoulder, hurried out with cries of--“Live the Bastille prisoner!
en: Lorry saw the Doctor, surrounded by the crowd and walking in the middle of a line of twenty men holding hands and shoulders, being hurried out. The crowd shouted, “Long live the Bastille prisoner!

raw: Help for the Bastille prisoner’s kindred in La Force!
en: Help the Bastille prisoner's relative in La Force!

raw: Room for the Bastille prisoner in front there!
en: Make way for the Bastille prisoner!

raw: Save the prisoner Evrémonde at La Force!” and a thousand answering shouts.
en: Save the prisoner Evremonde at La Force!” along with thousands of answering cheers.

raw: He closed the lattice again with a fluttering heart, closed the window and the curtain, hastened to Lucie, and told her that her father was assisted by the people, and gone in search of her husband.
en: With a beating heart, Mr. Lorry closed the shutter, the window, and the curtain. He ran to Lucie and told her that her father had the help of the crowd and had gone to find her husband.

raw: He found her child and Miss Pross with her; but, it never occurred to him to be surprised by their appearance until a long time afterwards, when he sat watching them in such quiet as the night knew.
en: He found her child and Miss Pross with her, though it did not occur to him to wonder how they had arrived until much later, when he sat watching them in the quiet night.

raw: Lucie had, by that time, fallen into a stupor on the floor at his feet, clinging to his hand.
en: By that time, Lucie had collapsed onto the floor at his feet, holding his hand in a daze.

raw: Miss Pross had laid the child down on his own bed, and her head had gradually fallen on the pillow beside her pretty charge.
en: Miss Pross had put the child to sleep on his bed and rested her head on the pillow next to her.

raw: O the long, long night, with the moans of the poor wife! And O the long, long night, with no return of her father and no tidings!
en: It was a long, terrible night, filled with the quiet cries of the poor wife, with no sign of her father and no news of Charles!

raw: Twice more in the darkness the bell at the great gate sounded, and the irruption was repeated, and the grindstone whirled and spluttered. “What is it?” cried Lucie, affrighted. “Hush!
en: Twice more during the night, the gate bell rang, the crowd rushed in, and the grindstone spun and sparked again. “What is that?” Lucie asked in terror. “Hush!

raw: The soldiers’ swords are sharpened there,” said Mr.
en: They are sharpening the soldiers' swords,” Mr.

raw: Lorry. “The place is national property now, and used as a kind of armoury, my love.”
en: Lorry said. “The building belongs to the nation now, and they are using it as a workshop, my love.”

raw: Twice more in all; but, the last spell of work was feeble and fitful.
en: Those were the only times, and the last session of sharpening was short and quiet.

raw: Soon afterwards the day began to dawn, and he softly detached himself from the clasping hand, and cautiously looked out again.
en: Soon dawn broke, and Mr. Lorry gently let go of Lucie's hand and looked out the window again.

raw: A man, so besmeared that he might have been a sorely wounded soldier creeping back to consciousness on a field of slain, was rising from the pavement by the side of the grindstone, and looking about him with a vacant air.
en: A man covered in blood and dirt, looking like a wounded soldier waking up on a battlefield, got up from the ground near the grindstone and looked around blankly.

raw: Shortly, this worn-out murderer descried in the imperfect light one of the carriages of Monseigneur, and, staggering to that gorgeous vehicle, climbed in at the door, and shut himself up to take his rest on its dainty cushions.
en: Soon, this exhausted killer saw one of the nobleman's carriages parked in the yard. Staggering over to the fancy carriage, he climbed inside and shut the door to sleep on its soft cushions.

raw: The great grindstone, Earth, had turned when Mr.
en: The earth had turned, and the sun cast a red glow over the courtyard when Mr.

raw: Lorry looked out again, and the sun was red on the courtyard.
en: Mr. Lorry looked out the window again, and the sun cast a red glow over the courtyard.

raw: But, the lesser grindstone stood alone there in the calm morning air, with a red upon it that the sun had never given, and would never take away.
en: But the other grindstone stood alone in the quiet morning air, stained with a red color that the sun had not created, and would never wash away.
